title: Total variation distance via the density's L¹-deviation from one
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and suppose that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$. Then the total variation distance between $\mu$ and $
u$ equals one half of the density absolute integral, that is,
\[
\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u) =  rac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega} \left|  rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) - 1 ight| \, d
u(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ is a probability measure on Ω
ν is a probability measure on Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
